questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

In this cold weather, / there’s nothing / like good / cup of coffee.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the omission of the article "**a**" before the term "**good cup of coffee**."
 
• Singular countable nouns typically require an article** ("a" or "an").**
 
• The correct phrase should be "**like a good cup of coffee**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 3** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"In this cold weather, there’s nothing** like a good **cup of coffee."*

• **4) there’s nothing** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

⇒ Total days to complete the work = 24 / 6

questions.question: What is the use of Net National Product (NNP)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To calculate per capita income **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is an important economic indicator that reflects the total value of all goods and services

 
 
• produced by a country’s citizens and businesses, both domestically and abroad
 
 
 
• The use of Net National Product is to calculate per capita income.
 
• Net National Product (NNP):
 
 
• NNP is obtained by subtracting depreciation value (i.e. capital stock consumption) from GNP.
 
 
 
• NNP reflects the true net income of an economy, it helps governments and businesses in planning for the long term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Gross Domestic Product (GDP):

 
 
• It is the total money value of all final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of the country during a given period of time.
 
• GDP = C + G + I
 
 
• C = Consumption expenditure
 
• G = Government expenditure
 
• I = Investment expenditure
 
 
 
 
 
• Gross National Product (GNP):
 
 
• It refers to the money value of the total output of production of final goods and services produced by the nationals of a country during a given period of time, generally a year.
 
 
 
• National Income (NI):
 
 
• When NNP is calculated at factor cost (FC) it is called National Income.
 
• The measure is calculated by deducting indirect taxes and adding subsidies in NNP at Market Price (MP).
 
• In India, the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is the weighted average price of 676 items with the base year 2017-18.

questions.question: The Supreme Court, in May 2023, observed that it can give divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage by exercising its discretionary power under ________.

options.text: Article 142 of the Constitution of India
Article 136 of the Constitution of India
Article 143 of the Constitution of India
Article 32 of the Constitution of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 142 of the Constitution of India**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In May 2023, the Supreme Court of India used Article 142(1) of the Indian Constitution to grant couples the right to divorce based on 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage'.
 
• Article 142(1) of the Indian Constitution reads, "The Supreme Court in the exercise of its jurisdiction may pass such decree or make such order as is necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it...".
 
• The Supreme Court's decision expanded the grounds on which divorce can be sought in India.
 
• Previously, the grounds for divorce were outlined in individual personal laws and did not include the concept of 'irretrievable breakdown of marriage' as it was not explicitly listed as grounds for divorce in any specific legislation. The 2023 ruling made it a valid reason to seek a divorce.
 
• The court used its discretionary powers to take cognizance of the realities of irreparable marriages and rule in favor of allowing legal terminations in such cases. This action sets a significant precedent for future cases involving such marital situations.
 
• This step by the Supreme Court could potentially pave the way for broader legal reform, rooting the law more firmly in the changing social context and conditions of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 136 – Special Leave to Appeal to the Supreme Court****​**

 
 
• It Grants the Supreme Court discretionary power to allow special leave to appeal against any judgment, decree, or order in any cause or matter, passed by any court or tribunal.
 
• This article applies to both civil and criminal cases, giving broad powers to the Supreme Court to ensure justice.
 
• It cannot be used for appeals from judgments of military courts or tribunals.
 
 
 
• **Article 143 – Power of the President to Consult the Supreme Court**
 
 
• It Empowers the President of India to seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on any question of law or fact of public importance.
 
• The Supreme Court's advice is not binding on the President; it is a consultative process.
 
• **It is ** Used to clarify constitutional or legal issues, like the Ayodhya case and the Berubari case.
 
 
 
• **Article 32** – **Right to Constitutional Remedies**
 
 
• **​It is one of the Fundamental Rights.**
 
• **It is the Heart and Soul of the Constitution.**
 
• It Empowers individuals to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.

The correct answer is __**Article 3**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Constitution (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1955 amended several articles of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **One significant change was the amendment to Article 3.**
 
• It d**eals with the procedure for the formation of new states **and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
 
• The amendment clarified and reinforced the process by which the Parliament could enact changes concerning the states.
 
• It made it explicit that the President of India could initiate the process of reorganization, and the Parliament would then have the final say.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 17: Abolition of Untouchability**

 
 
• **​A**bolishes the practice of untouchability, making it illegal in India.
 
• It states that the enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability is a punishable offense under the law.
 
• The article promotes social equality by ensuring that all individuals have the right to equality before the law, irrespective of caste.
 
 
 
• **Article 34: Restriction on Rights Conferred by Part III While Martial Law is in Force**
 
 
• **​A**llows the Parliament to restrict the rights conferred by Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Constitution during the enforcement of martial law in any area.
 
 
 
• **Article 45: Provision for Early Childhood Care and Education**
 
 
• **​D**irects the state to provide for early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.
 
• Emphasizes the importance of early childhood education in the holistic development of children,
 
 
• addressing their physical, mental, and social needs.

questions.question: What is known to be ‘ekaharya’, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Bharatnatyam dance is a dance form of Tamil Nadu which is also known to be as ekaharya, where one dancer takes on several roles in a single performance.
 
• It is also known as Dasiattam.
 
• The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur has been a centre for Bharatanatyam since 1000 CE.
 
• In its usual form, the dance is generally divided into seven main parts – Alarippu, Jatiswaran, Shabda, Varna, Pada, Thillana and Sloka.
 
• Mrinalini Sarabhai, Shobhana, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, and Chithra Vishveshwaran 
 
 
• ​are some of the famous contemporaries of the Bharatnatyam Dance form.

• Kathak:​

 
 
• ​This dance originated in North India.
 
• It was largely a temple or village performance wherein the dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures.
 
 
 
• Kuchipudi:
 
 
• Kuchipudi is the name of a village in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh which has a long custom of dance-drama.
 
 
 
• Kathakali:
 
 
• Kathakali is a blend of dance, music, and acting and dramatizes stories, which are mostly adapted from Indian epics
 
• Different facial colors indicate different mental stages & characters, e.g. green – nobility, black – wicked, red patches – combining royalty & evil.

questions.question: How can you access the Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard in Microsoft Word?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clicking on the Mailings tab **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• **Step by Step Instructions **

 
 
• **Open Microsoft Word**:

 
 
• Launch Microsoft Word on your computer.
 
 
 
• **Go to the Mailings Tab:**
 
 
• At the top of the window, find and click on the "Mailings" tab in the ribbon.
 
 
 
• **Start Mail Merge**:
 
 
• In the "Mailings" tab, look for the "Start Mail Merge" group.
 
• Click on "Start Mail Merge" to see a dropdown menu.
 
 
 
• **Select Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard**:
 
 
• From the dropdown menu, select **"Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard..."**.
 
• This will open the Mail Merge task pane on the right side of your Word window.
 
 
 
• **Follow the Wizard**:
 
 
• The wizard guide you through the mail merge process with clear steps,
 
 
• including selecting the document type, choosing recipients, writing the letter, and completing the merge.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Green Revolution is/are correct?

I. India became self-reliant after the advent of the Green Revolution.

II. Due to the Green Revolution, the soil started losing nutrients due to repeated cultivation of the same crop.

III. Green revolution caused depletion of fresh ground water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i, ii and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India led to self-reliance in terms of food grain production, transforming the country from a food-deficient nation to one that could sustain itself.
 
• Repetitive cultivation of the same high-yield variety (HYV) crops led to soil nutrient depletion, as these crops absorbed specific nutrients in large quantities.
 
• The Green Revolution intensified the use of water resources for irrigation, leading to the depletion of fresh groundwater levels, especially in regions like Punjab and Haryana.
 
• The use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides increased significantly during the Green Revolution, contributing to environmental degradation and impacting soil health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period during the 1960s and 1970s when agriculture in many developing countries was transformed by the adoption of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• It aimed to increase food production to combat hunger and improve food security.
 
• Countries like India and Mexico saw significant increases in crop production, particularly in wheat and rice.
 
• Despite its success in increasing food production, the Green Revolution also led to environmental issues, including soil degradation, water scarcity, and loss of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Soil Nutrient Depletion:**
 
 
• Continuous cultivation of the same crop without crop rotation can lead to the depletion of specific nutrients in the soil.
 
• This results in reduced soil fertility, necessitating the increased use of chemical fertilizers to maintain crop yields.
 
• Over time, this can lead to soil degradation and reduced agricultural sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Groundwater Depletion:**
 
 
• Intensive irrigation practices, particularly in regions with limited water resources, can lead to the over-extraction of groundwater.
 
• This can cause a decline in water tables, making it more difficult and expensive to access water for irrigation in the long term.
 
• Regions like Punjab and Haryana in India have experienced significant groundwater depletion due to the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The increased use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides associated with the Green Revolution has led to environmental pollution.
 
• These chemicals can contaminate soil and water bodies, adversely affecting plant and animal life.
 
• There are also health concerns for humans exposed to these chemicals through food and water.

questions.question: What was the Child Sex Ratio in the country as per the Census of India 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**919.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the census 2001, the child sex ratio of India was 927 which declined to 919 in the census 2011. 
 
• Child sex ratio:
 
 
• The Child Sex Ratio is defined as the number of females per 1000 males in the age group 0–6 years.
 
 
 
• As per the census 2011, Arunachal Pradesh has the highest child sex ratio among the Indian states i.e. 972 while Haryana has the lowest child sex ratio i.e., 834 per thousand males. 
 
• Among the Union Territories of India; Andaman and Nicobar Islands has the highest child sex ratio i.e., 968 per thousand males. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The responsibility of conducting the decennial Census rests with the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• Census Act was enacted in 1948 to provide for the scheme of conducting population census with duties and responsibilities of census officers.
 
• Government of India decided in May 1949 to initiate steps for developing systematic collection of statistics on the size of the population, its growth, etc., and established an organisation in the Ministry of Home Affairs under Registrar General and ex-Officio Census Commissioner, India.

questions.question: Which of the following types of music is confined to the states of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Carnatic**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carnatic Music__

 __
 
• Carnatic music is one of the forms of Indian classical music.
 
• It is confined to southern India, the states of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamilnadu, and Kerala
 
 
• ​ while the classical music of the rest of the country is under the name of Hindustani.
 
 
 
• The main emphasis in Carnatic music is on the vocals.
 
• The music is created in the traditional octave form and the music is Kriti-based
 
 
• ​ and focuses more on the Sahithya or the lyric quality of the musical piece.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Music**

 
 
• **​**Hindustani music is a major form of classical music practised primarily in North India, dating back to the Vedic times.
 
• It is based on **ragas** (melodic frameworks) and **talas** (rhythmic cycles) with a strong emphasis on improvisation by the performer.
 
• Renowned figures like **Pandit Ravi Shankar**, **Ustad Zakir Hussain**, and **Kishori Amonkar** have popularized Hindustani music globally.
 
• Common instruments include the **sitar**, **tabla**, **sarod**, and **tanpura**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Music**
 
 
• **​**Regional music refers to folk and traditional music from different parts of India, reflecting the cultural diversity of various regions.
 
• **Bihu** (Assam), **Baul** (Bengal), **Lavani** (Maharashtra), and **Garba** (Gujarat) are popular forms of regional music.
 
• Unlike classical music, regional music often has simpler structures, with repetitive rhythms and lyrics rooted in everyday life
 
 
 
• **Classical Music**
 
 
• **​**Indian classical music is divided into two main traditions: **Hindustani (North Indian)** and **Carnatic (South Indian)**.
 
• Classical music often has spiritual undertones, used in temples and courts historically, and is meditative in nature.
 
• Well-known classical musicians include **MS Subbulakshmi** (Carnatic), **Bismillah Khan** (Shehnai), and **Zakir Hussain** (Tabla).

questions.question: Since 1994, Winter Olympics traditionally take place _____ after the Summer Olympics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 years**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Since 1994, the Winter Olympics traditionally take place **two years** after the Summer Olympics. 
 
• This change was introduced to alternate the Winter and Summer Olympics every two years, instead of holding them in the same year as was done earlier.
 
• It is a sporting event that occurs every four years.
 
• The first celebration of the Winter Olympics was held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.
 
• The original sports were alpine and cross-country skiing, figure skating, ice hockey, Nordic combined, ski jumping, and speed skating.
 
• The Games were held every four years from 1924 until 1936, after which they were interrupted by World War II.
 
• The Olympics resumed in 1948 and were celebrated every four years.
 
• The Winter and Summer Olympic Games were held in the same years until 1992, after a 1986 decision by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to place the Summer and Winter Games on separate four-year cycles in alternating even-numbered years.
 
• Because of the change, the next Winter Olympics after 1992 was in 1994.
 
• The 2022 Winter Olympics, officially known as the XXIV Olympic Winter Games and commonly known as Beijing 2022, is an international winter multi-sport event that is scheduled to take place from 4 to 20 February 2022, in Beijing and towns in the neighboring Hebei province in the People's Republic of China. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 2020 Summer Olympics commonly known as Tokyo 2020, is to be held in Tokyo, Japan.
 
• Hockey, Badminton, and Archery are the summer Olympic sports.
 
• Karate, roller sport, climbing, surfing, baseball, and softball are the recent sports added for 2020.
 
• Beijing is due to host the 2022 Winter Olympics, which will make it the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Games.
